requirements.text: Make her close her jacket fully

outcomes.description: The woman's jacket is closed completely.
outcomes.target: The jacket is fully closed, with its front panels brought together and no visible opening remaining along the closure.
outcomes.reference: The woman's jacket in the input image.

nodes.question: Compared with the source image, is there clear visible evidence that the same woman's jacket has been brought closer together along its front closure in the edited image?
nodes.criteria: Pass only if the source/edit comparison clearly shows some progress toward closing the jacket, even if a visible opening remains. Fail only if the closure is clearly assessable and shows no progress or is more open. Unknown if the changed pose, drape, or occlusion prevents a reliable comparison; low confidence alone is not sufficient for unknown.
nodes.binding: Assess the same woman's jacket in both images. Use the source to identify the garment and compare its front closure; do not infer closure from silhouette or drape. This check concerns progress, not complete fulfillment.

nodes.question: In the edited image, is the same woman's jacket fully closed, with no visible opening remaining along its front closure?
nodes.criteria: Pass only if the front panels meet along the entire visible closure and no opening remains. Fail if a visible opening remains or the closure is clearly not fully closed. Unknown if the closure is obscured or cannot be judged from the edited image; do not infer failure from low confidence alone.
nodes.binding: Assess the same woman's jacket identified in s1. Judge the edited image's visible front closure; the source is for garment identification, not a substitute for evidence of the edited endpoint. Full closure is required; partial closure is not complete fulfillment.

nodes.question: Is the woman's jacket fully closed?
nodes.criteria: Complete only when s2 passes. Partial when s2 does not pass and s1 passes, establishing progress without full closure. Absent only when s1 fails and s2 fails with clear evidence that no requested progress occurred. Unknown whenever necessary evidence is unresolved, including an unknown s1 or s2; do not convert uncertainty into absence.

program.checker_template:
Execute ONE saved check. Return status, evidence, confidence (0 to 1 or null), and used_dependency_ids. You receive no reference label or optimizer feedback. Do not predict what the optimizer wants.
Support checks receive source and edited images. Inspect only the saved visual proposition and binding. When dependencies are supplied, use those ancestor observations as context and investigate the more specific proposition yourself; do not simply repeat the parent answer. Use pass/fail/unknown. A pass on a broad parent does not imply a nested check passes. Known negative evidence is usable; uncertain or missing evidence is unknown. Do not award requested completion credit to supporting facts.
The requested fulfillment readout receives NO images. Use ALL and ONLY saved support observations, the original instruction, rubric and saved composition criteria. Use complete/partial/absent/unknown. Mere texture or object presence must not silently establish whole-image conversion or a requested spatial relation. Known progress plus evidenced incompleteness may be partial; absence means no requested progress. Missing necessary evidence is unknown, never a fabricated failure or completion. Do not infer new visual facts.
used_dependency_ids must name every supplied dependency check_id exactly once in saved order (empty when none). Confidence is self-report, not calibrated correctness.

findings.question: Does the edited image provide enough visible evidence to determine whether the jacket’s front closure is fully closed, rather than merely appearing closed or open because of the woman’s turned pose and the jacket’s drape?
findings.criteria: Inspect the visible front closure itself. Pass only if the panels meet along the visible closure with no opening; fail only if an opening is clearly visible. If the turned pose or drape prevents judging the closure, mark unknown.
findings.evidence: In the edited image, the woman is turned sideways and the jacket hangs outward; the front closure is not clearly presented. The saved checks repeatedly describe it as visibly open, but do not resolve whether the apparent separation is an opening along the closure or a consequence of the pose and drape.
findings.rationale: The endpoint check is central to the request, but its fail observations may overstate what can be inferred from the oblique, draped view. A focused check of the closure itself would distinguish clear incompleteness from insufficient visual evidence. The source shows the jacket front more directly, but does not establish the edited endpoint.
